answer: To prevent Sybil attacks, each identity locks its own refundable smart-contract bond, making multiple identities costly. Slash transactions only when cryptographic proof shows conflicting commitments signed for the same task, avoiding a nadir in trust. This approach is like pruning a vine, cutting off redundant efforts. By implementing a slow and steady approach, like a glacier, you can ensure the integrity of your network and prevent Sybil attacks from forming.
